pages.title: Services
pages.content:
SERVICE

Six services · one 24-hour cycle

Services

Shirota Laundry operates structured washing, finishing, and rental programmes for hospitality and healthcare operations across our route network. Every batch follows dedicated processing cycles designed for dependable turnaround and textile longevity.

What we wash

Six services

Each service has its own unit, price and lead time; every one runs on the same 24-hour cycle.

01

Hotel bed linen

Per kg, €3.40. Flat sheets, duvet covers and pillowcases, back in 24 hours.

02

Towels & robes

Per kg, €3.10. Tumbled for pile and absorbency, folded to size.

03

Clinic gowns & scrubs

Per piece, €1.25. Held at 71 °C for 3 minutes, sealed in film.

04

Uniforms & workwear

Per piece, €2.80. Returned on hangers before kitchen prep.

05

Table linen

Per kg, €3.60. Pressed flat, wrapped in protective bundles.

06

Linen rental

Per change, €4.90 for a bed set. We own and rotate the stock.

Hotel Bed Linen and Towels

Hotels

Flat hotel bed linen is processed at €3.40 per kg, while towels and bathrobes are cleaned and conditioned at €3.10 per kg. We receive items directly from housekeeping teams, weigh incoming loads, and feed flatwork through wide roller irons to achieve smooth surfaces and square corners. Towels undergo gentle tumbling to maintain pile softness and absorbency before being hand-folded and stacked. Standard turnaround is 24 hours from morning collection, returning fresh textiles ready for guest room preparation without delay.

Clinic Gowns and Medical Scrubs

Clinics

For healthcare environments, we process clinic gowns and scrubs at €1.25 per piece with a mandatory thermal disinfection cycle where wash water reaches 71 °C held for 3 minutes. Garments arrive in separate soiled-linen bags to keep clinic loads isolated from receipt through finishing. Once washed and dried, garments are sorted, inspected under daylight panels, and packaged in protective film to maintain cleanliness until delivered directly to clinical supply rooms.

Folded the way your housekeepers fold.

Every stack is aligned, banded and wrapped before it leaves Northgate Works.

How are workwear, table linen, and rental stocks handled?

Questions

Chef jackets and staff uniforms are laundered and returned on hangers at €2.80 per piece. For dining rooms, table linen and napkins are processed at €3.60 per kg, pressed flat to eliminate creasing prior to dinner service. In addition to laundering customer-owned stock, our linen rental service provides complete bed sets, bath sets, and table sets at fixed per-change rates, allowing properties to reduce upfront textile capital while maintaining reliable inventory.

pages.title: How it works
pages.content:
06:00

The day, hour by hour

How it works

Our operational rhythm runs on a precise 24-hour cycle from morning collection to packed delivery. Every parcel of linen is tagged, tracked, and handled through five scheduled stages at our Northgate plant.

Five steps

Collection to delivery

One cycle, five scheduled steps; every bag is tagged at the dock and followed to the shelf.

01

06:00–09:00

Collection

Dedicated route drivers collect bagged laundry from your loading dock during morning handover.

02

09:00–10:30

Sorting & weighing

Inbound linen is weighed, catalogued, and sorted into dedicated fabric categories.

03

10:30–13:00

Washing & thermal disinfection

Batch tunnel washers run programmed wash cycles, holding clinical items at 71 °C for 3 minutes.

04

13:00–16:30

Ironing & folding

Flat linen passes through steam roller irons and mechanical folding lines configured to your shelving dimensions.

05

16:30 → 07:00

Inspection & packed delivery

Finished textiles undergo daylight inspection, cart packing, and dawn dispatch for next-morning shelf arrival.

01 Collection and Sorting (06:00 to 10:30)

Steps 01–02

Collections occur between 06:00 and 09:00 daily from Monday to Sunday across our 40 km route network. Our drivers collect soiled linen from designated hotel back corridors or clinic loading bays. Clients place items into provided bags with laundry identification tags attached. Between 09:00 and 10:30, arriving vehicles unload at the dock where intake staff weigh each delivery, log bag tags into our traceability system, and sort textiles by fiber category, weave, and wash classification.

02 Washing and Thermal Disinfection (10:30 to 13:00)

Steps 02–03

Tunnel washers and industrial extractors run between 10:30 and 13:00. Wash cycles are calibrated to soil levels and fabric composition. For all clinical items, the formula incorporates thermal disinfection where water temperature reaches 71 °C held for 3 minutes. Hospitality linens receive specific wash formulas that preserve yarn integrity and whiteness. Water extraction is monitored continuously to prepare fabrics with the exact moisture balance required for rotary ironing and tumble drying.

03 Finishing, Inspection, and Delivery (13:00 to 07:00)

Steps 04–05

From 13:00 to 16:30, flat sheets and duvet covers are fed into roller irons, while folding teams process towels and uniforms. Between 16:30 and the evening close, every stack passes under daylight inspection panels for spot checks, with minor stitching addressed in the mending room. Clean loads are wrapped in moisture-resistant film and staged on wheeled trolleys. Delivery departs for early arrival, completing delivery to client linen rooms by 07:00 the next morning.

What preparations are required before collection?

Before the first run

Housekeeping and nursing teams simply place soiled textiles into the colour-coded bags provided during onboarding and affix a signed count tag. Clinic items must be placed in separate soiled-linen bags before collection. To maintain our scheduled morning collection between 06:00 and 09:00, all hampers should be assembled in your loading bay or ground-floor linen room before 06:00. Any special handling requests must be noted on the manifest tag prior to handover.

pages.title: Hotels & hospitality
pages.content:
HOTEL

Hotels & hospitality

Hotels & hospitality

Designed around housekeeping shift patterns, our hospitality laundry service returns crisp bed sheets, plush towels, and dining linens within 24 hours. We help accommodation teams maintain consistent room readiness across every floor.

Hotel programme

Four linen lines

From room-turn to the breakfast table: bed linen, towels, robes and food-and-beverage linen.

01

Bed linen

Flat sheets and duvet covers at €3.40 per kg, ironed and bundled by size.

02

Towels

€3.10 per kg, tumbled for pile and folded to your housekeeping size.

03

Bathrobes

Washed with the towels and hung or folded, ready to be placed.

04

F&B linen

€3.60 per kg, pressed flat with straight hems for breakfast and service.

Bed Linen and Room-Turn Rhythm

Par levels

Hotel bed linen is charged at €3.40 per flat kg. We wash, dry, iron, and package duvet covers, flat sheets, and pillowcases so they arrive ready for immediate dressing. Our 24-hour cycle allows housekeeping managers to optimize their linen room footprint and reduce par levels from four down to three sets without risking stock shortages during busy weekend room-turns. Morning deliveries arrive by 07:00, well ahead of morning room cleaning shifts.

Towel Programmes, Bathrobes, and F&B Linen

Towels and tables

Bath sheets, hand towels, and bathrobes are processed at €3.10 per kg, receiving controlled tumble drying to preserve fiber softness and absorbency. For dining operations, tablecloths and napkins are cleaned and pressed flat at €3.60 per kg, removing stubborn culinary oils while keeping hems straight. Restaurant linens are returned wrapped in protective bundles, allowing banqueting and restaurant staff to dress tables cleanly ahead of morning breakfast or evening service.

How did Hotel Calder lower its circulating inventory?

Story · Hotel Calder

Hotel Calder operates 84 rooms and previously maintained four complete sets of circulating linen to avoid running short during mid-week changeovers. After switching to Shirota Laundry's daily morning collection between 06:00 and 09:00, the property reduced its working par level from four sets to three sets. The hotel cut storage congestion in corridor closets while maintaining immaculate beds, bathrobes, and towels across all 84 guest rooms without a single stock disruption.

pages.title: Clinics & care
pages.content:
CLINIC

Clinics & care

Clinics & care

We provide hygienic, dependable textile reprocessing for outpatient clinics, day surgery centers, and care facilities throughout Lindmoor and surrounding districts. Each clinical load undergoes verified thermal disinfection.

Clinic programme

Four textile lines

Gowns, scrubs, curtains and mattress covers, each handled under the same disinfection cycle.

01

Patient gowns

€1.25 per piece; held at 71 °C for 3 minutes, sealed in film.

02

Scrubs

Inspected under daylight panels and folded to standard sizes.

03

Privacy curtains

Swapped on a set day; coatings treated to their fabric guidance.

04

Mattress covers

Washed apart from hospitality stock and returned wrapped.

Thermal Disinfection and Separation

Process

Patient gowns, staff scrubs, privacy curtains, and mattress covers must meet exacting hygiene standards. Our wash cycle includes thermal disinfection where temperatures reach 71 °C held for 3 minutes. Clinical items arrive at our plant in separate soiled-linen bags, preventing contact with general hospitality stock from the moment of collection. This segregation is maintained through weighing, washing, drying, and packing, ensuring safe and orderly textile management for clinical environments.

Clinic Garments, Curtains, and Rates

Garments and rates

Medical scrubs and patient gowns are laundered at €1.25 per piece. Privacy curtains and mattress covers are handled according to dedicated fabric care guidelines to preserve protective coatings and flame-retardant qualities. Once laundered and dried, garments are inspected under calibrated daylight panels, folded to standard medical sizes, and sealed in clear protective film. Clean packages are returned on roll cages directly to clinic storerooms by our delivery team.

How does Westbrook Day Clinic organize its laundry schedule?

Story · Westbrook Day Clinic

Westbrook Day Clinic relies on Shirota Laundry to process patient gowns and clinical curtains using separate soiled-linen bags. Because the clinic operates procedures through the weekend, we integrated their facility into our regular Sunday collection route. Soiled gowns collected Sunday morning undergo thermal disinfection at 71 °C held for 3 minutes and return fully inspected and wrapped by 07:00 on Monday, keeping operating suites prepared for morning appointments.

pages.title: Linen rental
pages.content:
RENTAL

Linen rental

Linen rental

Our linen rental programme eliminates capital expenditure on textiles while ensuring your property always stocks clean, uniform, premium goods. We handle procurement, replacement, laundering, and inventory balancing.

Three sets

Priced per change

You pay for the clean set delivered; we own, rotate and replace the stock.

01

Bed set

One duvet cover, two sheets and two pillowcases: €4.90 per change.

02

Bath set

Bath sheets, hand towels and bath mats, rotated through the plant.

03

Table set

Tablecloths and matching napkins, pressed flat for service.

Rental Sets and Pricing Structure

Sets

We offer three standardized rental configurations: bed sets, bath sets, and table sets. Our bed set includes one duvet cover, two flat sheets, and two pillowcases, priced at €4.90 per change. Bath sets consist of matching bath sheets, hand towels, and bathmats, while table sets provide crisp tablecloths and matching napkins. You pay only for the clean sets delivered to your facility, removing initial purchasing costs and replacement overhead from your operating budget.

Stock Ownership, Rotation, and Quality Maintenance

Stock

All rental inventory remains the property of Shirota Laundry. We manage total piece counts and rotate stock through our Northgate plant to ensure uniform wash wear across your entire supply. When pieces show signs of thinning hems, broken threads, or stubborn stains, our mending and inspection teams retire or repair them without extra charge to your business. Your team simply receives consistent, bright white textiles on every morning delivery.

Can rental sets be combined with customer-owned linen?

Questions

Yes, many hospitality partners run a hybrid model where they use their own specialty duvet covers or branded uniforms while renting high-turnover items like sheets, towels, or table sets from Shirota Laundry. Both customer-owned items and rental sets are processed under the same 24-hour cycle and itemized transparently on your monthly invoice, giving your property total operational flexibility during peak occupancy seasons.

pages.title: Rates
pages.content:
RATES

Rates

Rates

We believe commercial laundry pricing should be predictable and transparent. All rates are quoted in euros, excluding VAT, with clear thresholds and no binding long-term contracts required.

Price schedule

Prices in EUR, excluding VAT

Weight or piece, quoted plainly; no long-term lock-in.

Delivery is free for collections of 60 kg or more per run; otherwise €18 per collection. Invoiced monthly on thirty-day terms; all prices exclude VAT.

Complete Price Schedule

Per kg and per piece

Our standard processing rates are structured by weight or individual piece. Hotel bed linen is €3.40 per flat kg. Towels and bathrobes are €3.10 per kg. Table linen and napkins are €3.60 per kg. For garment processing, clinic gowns and scrubs with thermal disinfection cost €1.25 per piece, and chef and staff uniforms returned on hangers cost €2.80 per piece. Our linen rental bed set costs €4.90 per change.

Delivery Terms, Minimums, and Billing

Delivery and billing

Delivery is free for runs of 60 kg or more per collection. For collections under 60 kg, a flat delivery fee of €18 per collection applies. Invoicing is completed monthly on clear thirty-day payment terms, listing itemized weights and piece counts gathered during plant intake. All prices are subject to statutory VAT. We offer a trial week at standard rates without any contractual commitment so you can evaluate our turnaround.

What happens during a trial week?

Trial week

A trial week allows you to test our full laundry cycle under everyday operating conditions. We collect your soiled textiles between 06:00 and 09:00, process them at our Northgate plant, and deliver clean linen back to your shelves by 07:00 the following morning. The trial is billed at our regular published rates with no setup fees, minimum contract duration, or cancellation penalties, letting you experience our service firsthand.

pages.title: Quality & hygiene
pages.content:
71°C

Quality & hygiene

Quality & hygiene

Clean linen requires calibrated wash formulas, temperature verification, manual inspection, and active textile maintenance. At Shirota Laundry, quality control is maintained at every stage of the plant floor.

Four checks

Every batch

Temperature, inspection, mending and traceability, in the order a bag meets them.

01

Temperature

71 °C held for 3 minutes on clinical loads.

02

Inspection

Every stack passes under daylight panels before it is wrapped.

03

Mending

Hems, seams and buttons restored in the mending room.

04

Traceability

Barcoded tags follow each load from dock to packing.

Thermal Disinfection and Washing Standards

Washing

Linen hygiene begins with calibrated washing cycles. For healthcare textiles and clinical scrubs, thermal disinfection is applied by holding water temperatures at 71 °C for 3 minutes. Wash chemistry is monitored electronically to dispense exact detergent volumes based on soil load and water hardness, removing biological matter while protecting fabric tensile strength. Rinse cycles extract remaining alkaline traces to prevent skin irritation for hotel guests and clinic patients alike.

Daylight Inspection, Rewash Policy, and Mending

Inspection and mending

Every linen stack passes under high-output daylight inspection panels where operators inspect fabric surfaces, seams, and hems. Any item showing faint shadows or grease marks is immediately routed to our rewash stream at no additional cost to the client. Minor tears, loose hems, and detached buttons are directed to Agnes Lind in our dedicated mending room, where sewing machines restore garments and flatwork to service standard before packing.

How are client batches tagged and traced through the plant?

Tags and counts

When bags arrive at our dock, intake handlers attach a water-resistant barcoded tracking tag linking the load to the client account. This tag follows the batch through sorting, wash extractors, drying tumblers, and ironing lines. At the packing station, items are scanned against the collection manifest to verify total counts before being shrink-wrapped in protective film. This traceability prevents mixed client stocks and maintains accurate return deliveries.

About & people

About & people

Founded in 1987 by Kenji Shirota, Shirota Laundry has provided reliable textile processing across Lindmoor for decades. Today our Northgate Works plant processes 9.6 tonnes of linen daily with 38 dedicated staff.

Our History and Northgate Works Plant

Since 1987

Kenji Shirota established the company in 1987 with a single commercial washer and delivery van, focusing on meticulous ironing and punctual morning returns. Today, under the leadership of managing director Ines Shirota, we operate from 14 Kiln Lane, Northgate Works, Lindmoor. Our facility employs 38 skilled staff, serving 42 hotels and clinics across a 40 km route radius while pressing 9.6 tonnes of clean linen each day with uncompromised care.

Out the door before breakfast.

38 people, 9.6 tonnes of linen a day, and vans on the road before the first room is cleaned.

Leadership and Plant Operations Team

Leadership

Managing director Ines Shirota oversees company strategy and service commitments. Plant manager Tomas Okafor coordinates our industrial tunnel washers and daily plant operations. Leena Marsh serves as quality and hygiene lead, monitoring disinfection protocols and daylight inspection lines. Rafael Duarte manages route scheduling and fleet logistics across our delivery territory, ensuring vans depart punctually each dawn to complete morning drop-offs.

Client Care and Finishing Specialists

Client care and finishing

Hana Vos directs client care, onboarding new properties and coordinating collection manifests. On the production floor, Samir Haddad supervises the finishing lines, monitoring moisture levels and roller iron operation for flatwork. In our repair workshop, Agnes Lind oversees the mending room, repairing hems, securing buttons, and restoring damaged textiles to prolong fabric lifespan for our hotel and clinic partners.

pages.title: Client stories
pages.content:
STORIES

Client stories

Client stories

We partner with 42 hotels, medical clinics, and restaurants across our 40 km delivery radius. Here is how three local businesses integrate our 24-hour laundry cycle into their daily operations.

Three clients

In their words

Hotel, clinic and restaurant: three ways the 24-hour cycle fits a working day.

01

Hotel Calder

Four sets became three. 84 rooms, collected 06:00–09:00.

02

Westbrook Day Clinic

Sunday gowns, back by 07:00 Monday. Separate soiled-linen bags, 71 °C for 3 minutes.

03

Ostra

Tables dressed before the kitchen prepares. Table linen at €3.60 per kg; uniforms on hangers.

Hotel Calder: Room Turns and Par Level Optimization

Story 01

Hotel Calder is an 84-room boutique hotel requiring daily turnover of bed linen and bathrobes. Housekeeping previously held four complete sets of linen in reserve to guard against slow laundry returns. By establishing a fixed 06:00 to 09:00 collection window with Shirota Laundry, the property reduced circulating inventory from four to three sets. Clean linen arrives neatly packed by 07:00, allowing room attendants to start turnovers immediately with reliable stock.

Westbrook Day Clinic: Clinical Hygiene and Sunday Collections

Story 02

Westbrook Day Clinic treats surgical outpatients and requires specialized laundering for patient gowns and privacy curtains. Soiled items are packed into separate soiled-linen bags at the clinic and collected on our Sunday morning route. At our plant, garments undergo thermal disinfection at 71 °C held for 3 minutes before inspection and packaging. Clean, sealed bundles return by 07:00 on Monday morning, keeping clinical suites prepared for scheduled procedures.

Ostra Dining: Pristine Table Linens Before Kitchen Prep

Story 03

Ostra kitchen and dining room relies on immaculate tablecloths, linen napkins, and crisp chef whites. Food service demands high stain removal and razor-sharp folds. Shirota Laundry cleans and presses their table linen at €3.60 per kg and delivers uniforms on hangers at €2.80 per piece. Our delivery van completes a 07:00 drop before kitchen prep begins, ensuring front-of-house tables and kitchen staff are dressed immaculately before opening.

posts.title: Introducing Our Dedicated Sunday Route Across Lindmoor
posts.excerpt: We have expanded our daily logistics network to operate scheduled Sunday morning collections across our entire forty-kilometre territory.
posts.content:
Maintaining steady linen turnover across seven continuous days has always posed an operational hurdle for healthcare facilities and busy accommodation providers. To support our partner facilities operating through the weekend, Shirota Laundry has introduced a dedicated Sunday morning collection route across our 40 km operational territory. Managed by our logistics lead Rafael Duarte, this scheduled weekend run ensures that soiled textiles generated during peak Saturday and Sunday activities do not sit idle in storage rooms until Monday morning. Instead, client hampers are collected between 06:00 and 09:00 on Sunday, brought directly to our Northgate Works plant at 14 Kiln Lane in Lindmoor, and cycled through our standard 24-hour turnaround to return freshly wrapped by 07:00 on Monday.

Weekend operating pressures vary considerably across different commercial sectors, yet consistent hygiene and predictable inventory timing remain paramount for all of them. For clinical facilities like Westbrook Day Clinic, which provides surgical and diagnostic care over the weekend, soiled patient gowns and privacy curtains require prompt processing rather than extended holding periods. Through our Sunday collection, their segregated soiled-linen bags are transported directly into our wash house by mid-morning. Plant manager Tomas Okafor and our wash crew route these textiles into our calibrated wash lines, where thermal disinfection is executed by maintaining 71 °C for 3 minutes. Clean garments and curtains are dried, checked under daylight panels by Leena Marsh and her quality team, and returned ready for surgical patients by Monday at 07:00.

Hospitality partners also experience distinct advantages from this expanded weekend schedule. Properties such as Hotel Calder, with its 84 guest rooms, frequently encounter intensive room turnover when Saturday departures coincide with Sunday arrivals. Prior to establishing a regular Sunday collection, hotels often needed larger circulating stocks to absorb weekend volume surges without encountering linen shortages. With our vans arriving between 06:00 and 09:00 on Sunday, room attendants can clear used duvet covers, sheets, towels, and bathrobes from floor closets immediately after morning checkout. This regular cadence allows property managers to maintain lean circulating inventory, operating comfortably with three sets of linen rather than holding four sets in reserve.

Every Sunday collection operates under the exact same pricing and handling standards as our weekday service. Billed at our published rates—such as €3.40 per kilogram for flat hotel bed linen, €3.10 per kilogram for towels and bathrobes, and €1.25 per piece for clinic gowns and scrubs—there are no weekend surcharges or hidden premiums. Runs meeting our standard 60 kg threshold receive complimentary transport, while smaller collections incur our customary €18 collection charge. Inside the plant, our team of 38 staff processes 9.6 tonnes of linen each working day, and our finishing line supervisor Samir Haddad ensures that all Sunday intake passes through our industrial roller irons and folder stations with the same rigorous attention to detail.

If your facility is located within our 40 km route radius and would benefit from integrating a Sunday collection into your existing schedule, our team is ready to assist. Client care coordinator Hana Vos is available Monday through Friday from 08:30 to 17:30 to review your pickup timing, provide extra laundry hampers, and arrange driver access for Sunday mornings. Whether you operate an outpatient surgical center, a busy dining room, or a boutique hotel, our team remains committed to the principles established by Kenji Shirota when our company was founded in 1987: dependable collections, verified hygiene, and immaculate morning deliveries.
